about: Every model Team may call, and which providers serve it, with why each is free. Hand-edited; the one source of truth. build.py turns it into Portkey configs (one per model, one per tier), LiteLLM's config.yaml and Portkey's conf.json, and refuses any served_by whose free is not 'yes' or 'allowance', any blocked or unknown provider, any OpenRouter id that is not a ':free' variant. Model rows researched 2026-10-26 from each provider's own pricing and terms pages (archived as git show before-fresh-start:litellm/free-models.json) and folded into one row per model on 2026-10-27. tier/order: which LiteLLM tier group the model serves and its priority there (1 first; higher orders only when lower ones are cooling down or failing). tier null = free but not routed; 'unrouted' says why, or 'unavailable' when no provider serves it today. served_by: the providers that serve the model, in Portkey's failover order; 'unavailable' entries are kept on record and skipped by build.py.

gateway.portkey_port_why: where the unpatched Portkey process listens (loopback); gateway-rs proxy listens on 'port', resolves config names and writes requests.jsonl, then forwards here
gateway.port_why: PLAN.md says 8787, but 127.0.0.1:8787 is held by the launchd job com.fullmoney.myprof-gateway (another project's node gateway, running since 2026-10-09). Change this number and rebuild to move; nothing else hardcodes it.

auto.about: tier-auto, the conversation router: Hermes's main model. The same complexity_router scores each new human ask and sends the conversation to Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 by name; both fall back to Haiku 5.5 (model_fallbacks). The work itself goes to subagents on tier-work. Eli asked for this on 2026-11-14: Claude for the conversation, the free models for subagent work.
auto.allowance_why: Eli, 2026-11-14: the conversation runs on Sonnet 5.5 or Opus 5.5 through the Max subscription bridge (free: allowance), never an API key; subagents and cron stay on the free tier-work
auto.tiers_why: complexity label -> catalog model. Of 163 fresh asks the router classified through 2026-11-14 (usage.db, the old tier-auto), 134 scored SIMPLE, 25 MEDIUM, 4 COMPLEX, 0 REASONING, so Sonnet takes most of the conversation and Opus the asks that score COMPLEX or REASONING. To give Opus more of it, map MEDIUM to claude-opus-5-5.
auto.efforts_why: reasoning_effort set with the model, replacing whatever the caller sent; the subscription bridge passes it on as the Claude reasoning effort
auto.default_tier_why: where a request goes when classification cannot run
auto.classification_mode_why: classify each new human ask and keep that decision for the tool-call turns that follow, so the conversation does not switch model mid-task
auto.context_compaction_why: Hermes compresses its own context; the router must not rewrite history behind it
auto.session_affinity_ttl_why: how long a held decision lasts with no traffic; matches policy.litellm.session_pin_ttl_s

auto.about: tier-work, the work router: LiteLLM's complexity_router (litellm/litellm/router_strategy/complexity_router) scores each request locally, with no model call, and sends it to one of the free tiers below. Hermes's subagents (delegation.model) and cron name tier-work; the conversation itself is tier-auto, the router above. The chosen tier then routes as usual (order, fallbacks, session pin). build.py writes each router as one auto_router deployment.
auto.tiers_why: complexity label -> catalog tier. SIMPLE goes to medium (at effort low): every Hermes turn carries its tool loop and 48k-55k input tokens (usage.db 2026-11-12), which gpt-oss-120b on Groq cannot take (6k input) and the small simple-tier models answer by talking instead of calling tools; tier-simple stays for Hermes's auxiliary lanes. MEDIUM goes to complex (2026-11-12): 40 of 42 fresh asks that day scored SIMPLE or MEDIUM and all ran their whole tool loop on north-mini-code (30B / 3B active), so anything past a simple ask now plans on the complex tier, which nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b heads since 2026-11-14 (gemini-3.8-flash: ok 1 of 14, 6 rate-limited, 69.8 s, moved last). REASONING goes to complex too: moving gemini-3.8-flash there left the reasoning tier only command-a-plus, a Cohere allowance, which a classifier may not choose; tier-reasoning stays callable by name and as a fallback. claude is left out: this router does the work, and that stays on free models; the conversation's router, tier-auto, is the one that spends the Max allowance
auto.efforts_why: reasoning_effort set with the tier, replacing whatever the caller sent, so how hard a model thinks follows the classification too; litellm/team/effort_clamp.py then moves it into what the chosen model accepts, and models without reasoning drop it
auto.default_tier_why: where a request goes when classification cannot run
auto.classification_mode_why: classify each new human ask and keep that decision for the tool-call turns that follow, so an agent loop does not switch model mid-task; 'every_request' classifies every turn
auto.context_compaction_why: Hermes compresses its own context; the router must not rewrite history behind it
auto.session_affinity_ttl_why: how long a held decision lasts with no traffic; matches policy.litellm.session_pin_ttl_s

model_fallbacks.about: routed model -> the models to try, in order, when it fails or is cooling down (LiteLLM router fallbacks, like tier_fallbacks but by model id). The conversation (tier-auto) names Sonnet and Opus by model, so this is their fallback.
model_fallbacks.claude_why: Eli, 2026-11-14: the conversation is Opus or Sonnet 5.5 with a fallback to Haiku 5.5

policy.about: How the gateway behaves, as opposed to what it may call. build.py validates every value and writes it into the Portkey configs and LiteLLM's config.yaml; litellm/team/run.sh reads session_pin_ttl_s. Change a value, run build.py, restart both launchd jobs.

portkey.mode_why: per model, over its served_by rows: 'fallback' tries them in order and moves on for on_status_codes; 'loadbalance' picks one per request by each row's weight (default 1) and does not fail over inside the request, so LiteLLM's retry and fallback do that instead
portkey.on_status_codes_why: Portkey only falls over on a listed status. A dead or revoked key is 401/403, an exhausted trial is 402, a model the provider no longer serves is 404, a target timeout is 408: every one means 'try the next provider'
portkey.retry_why: one in-target retry only for transient server errors; 408 and 429 go straight to the next provider
portkey.default_timeout_why: per provider attempt, unless the provider sets request_timeout_ms

litellm.routing_strategy_why: null leaves LiteLLM's default (simple-shuffle, with each model's order taking precedence); or one of least-busy, latency-based-routing, usage-based-routing, usage-based-routing-v2. cost-based-routing is refused: every cost here is 0
litellm.router_why: num_retries per model group before falling back; max_fallbacks tier fallbacks per request; a deployment that fails allowed_fails times in a minute is skipped for cooldown_time seconds; pre-call checks skip models whose context cannot hold the prompt
litellm.context_window_fallbacks_why: tier -> tiers to try when the prompt is too long for the tier, same shape as tier_fallbacks; empty means none
litellm.drop_params_why: strip request params a provider does not support instead of failing the call
litellm.session_pin_ttl_why: litellm/team/session_pin.py keeps a session on the model that last answered it for this long

agent_gate.why: litellm/team/agent_gate.py, on tier calls that carry tools: only tools:true models, then drop a model whose last window_hours of tool requests (at least min_samples) succeeded under min_ok_pct (rate limits excluded) or answered fresh asks with a tool call under min_fresh_tool_pct. Starting values set 2026-11-12 with no record yet; tune from usage.db (had_tools, fresh_ask, tool_call)
